verses.pali: Saṁyutta Nikāya 44.10
1. Abyākatavagga
Ānandasutta
Atha kho vacchagotto paribbājako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
verses.english: Then the wanderer Vacchagotta went up to the Buddha and exchanged greetings with him.

verses.pali: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho vacchagotto paribbājako bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:

verses.pali: “kiṁ nu kho, bho gotama, atthattā”ti?
Evaṁ vutte, bhagavā tuṇhī ahosi.
verses.english: But when he said this, the Buddha kept silent.

verses.pali: “Kiṁ pana, bho gotama, natthattā”ti?
Dutiyampi kho bhagavā tuṇhī ahosi.
verses.english: But for a second time the Buddha kept silent.

verses.pali: Atha kho vacchagotto paribbājako uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.
verses.english: Then the wanderer Vacchagotta got up from his seat and left.

verses.pali: Atha kho āyasmā ānando acirapakkante vacchagotte paribbājake bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: And then, not long after Vacchagotta had left, Venerable Ānanda said to the Buddha:

verses.pali: “kiṁ nu kho, bhante, bhagavā vacchagottassa paribbājakassa pañhaṁ puṭṭho na byākāsī”ti?
verses.english: “Sir, why didn’t you answer Vacchagotta’s question?”

verses.pali: “Ahañcānanda, vacchagottassa paribbājakassa ‘atthattā’ti puṭṭho samāno ‘atthattā’ti byākareyyaṁ, ye te, ānanda, samaṇabrāhmaṇā sassatavādā tesametaṁ saddhiṁ abhavissa.
verses.english: “Ānanda, when Vacchagotta asked me whether the self survives, if I had answered that ‘the self survives’ I would have been siding with the ascetics and brahmins who are eternalists.

verses.pali: Ahañcānanda, vacchagottassa paribbājakassa ‘natthattā’ti puṭṭho samāno ‘natthattā’ti byākareyyaṁ, ye te, ānanda, samaṇabrāhmaṇā ucchedavādā tesametaṁ saddhiṁ abhavissa.
verses.english: When Vacchagotta asked me whether the self does not survive, if I had answered that ‘the self does not survive’ I would have been siding with the ascetics and brahmins who are annihilationists.

verses.pali: Ahañcānanda, vacchagottassa paribbājakassa ‘atthattā’ti puṭṭho samāno ‘atthattā’ti byākareyyaṁ, api nu me taṁ, ānanda, anulomaṁ abhavissa ñāṇassa uppādāya:
verses.english: When Vacchagotta asked me whether the self survives, if I had answered that ‘the self survives’, would that have facilitated the arising of the knowledge that

verses.pali: ‘sabbe dhammā anattā’”ti?
“No hetaṁ, bhante”.
“Ahañcānanda, vacchagottassa paribbājakassa ‘natthattā’ti puṭṭho samāno ‘natthattā’ti byākareyyaṁ, sammūḷhassa, ānanda, vacchagottassa paribbājakassa bhiyyo sammohāya abhavissa:
verses.english: “When Vacchagotta asked me whether the self does not survive, if I had answered that ‘the self does not survive’, Vacchagotta—who is already confused—would have got even more confused, thinking:

verses.pali: ‘ahuvā me nūna pubbe attā, so etarahi natthī’”ti.
verses.english: ‘It seems that the self that I once had no longer survives.’”

verses.pali: Dasamaṁ.
